title: Orchid Labs - Discovery call - migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Intro + discovery on migration from OpenAI -> Redwood Dedicated. Customer runs chat & generation at 10M tokens/day, concerned about cost and latency variability; primary drivers: cost predictability, data isolation, and eval parity. Discussed vLLM/TGI compatibility, model variants, quantization, and on-prem options. Agreed to run a 2-week benchmark on small set of prompts and share security docs + pricing outline.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining - i'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Amir on success. how are we doing?
[00:08] Leon: good thanks, leon here. had a quick lunch sorry running a bit behind.
[00:12] Jordan: no worries. quick run through agenda - understand your current stack (openai + some on prem inference), pain points, security, and see if dedicated makes sense for migration.
[00:23] Sara: yeah we'll give background - we run a few products: customer chat, doc search + summarization, and a gen assistant used in the app. most traffic is chat.
[00:31] Maya: we care about cost predictability and also keeping user data private - so isolation is important.
[00:36] Ethan: and from infra, we want latency consistency; we see P95 spikes when openai has contention and it's impacting front-end SLAs.
[00:45] Priya: okay great. quick question on scale - leon, what roughly are you seeing in tokens/day and per-request sizes?
[00:52] Leon: roughly 10M tokens/day across ensemble, average request 600 tokens, peak concurrent around 120 rps.
[01:02] Priya: got it, that's helpful. is cost currently your top driver or is it more about security/SLAs?
[01:08] Sara: combination - cost is substantial but the unpredictability and data concerns are bigger. our legal team wants data not to be shared with third-party models in plain buckets.
[01:17] Jordan: understood. so Dedicated or Private could address isolation. we usually recommend Dedicated for teams that want predictable capacity and don't need full air-gapped on-prem. Private is available for stricter reg requirements.
[01:30] Victor (brief): question about model parity - we use gpt-4-ish models via openai, and we need output quality to match. how do we ensure parity?
[01:38] Priya: great question. we do model verifications - we can run side-by-side evals with your prompt set. also discuss vLLM/TGI compatibility — if you're running custom runtime, we can support common formats and containerized model variants.
[01:50] Sara: on that — we have some in-house infra running vLLM for lower cost, but results vary. are there any gotchas moving models from openai to hosted/dedicated redwood?
[02:01] Priya: a few things: tokenization differences, temperature/random seed behaviors, and sometimes tokenizer mismatch causes subtle output diffs; we include eval harness to detect regressions. quantization changes also can change phrasing.
[02:15] Leon: what's your recommended path? dedicated with the same open weights or using your curated open models?
[02:21] Jordan: usually we recommend first running the same model family you use on openai, if available, to check parity. then iterate with quantized variants to reduce cost. for OpenAI-proprietary models we do equivalent open replacements or partner models.
[02:34] Ethan: how much work to integrate with our auth and VPC? we need SAML SSO, KMS, and VPC peering.
[02:41] Amir: we have an onboarding checklist - SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, and we support VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. we can share the architecture doc and security pack.
[02:52] Jordan: i'll drop the SOC2 + ISO docs and typical network topology.
[02:56] Maya: timeline — we have a Q3 rollout target for a pilot if cost/quality checks out.
[03:03] Jordan: that sounds achievable. typical pilot is 2 weeks of benchmark traffic and then a phased rollout.
[03:09] Priya: for benchmarking we usually ask for ~5-10% of your traffic or a representative sample and a set of prompts for eval. we run side-by-side across model variants, measure latency P50/P95/P99, token cost, and note quality diffs.
[03:22] Leon: do you support running customer's own checkpoints or does it have to be through your model catalog?
[03:27] Priya: for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own model artifacts; we have supported formats and can help containerize. for hosted we use curated variants. BYOM (bring-your-own-model) flows are common for Dedicated.
[03:37] Sara: about vLLM and TGI — we saw that runtimes can behave differently; will Redwood's runtime match vLLM output?
[03:45] Priya: runtime differences exist; we treat the runtime as an execution environment — for parity we compare outputs from your vLLM runs to Redwood's runtime; sometimes tokenization or decode algorithms differ, we track those.
[03:58] Ethan: are there memory/kv cache differences that affect latency for chat?
[04:03] Priya: yes, our runtime manages KV cache and has optimizations for attention and continuous batching; depending on sequence lengths and window sizes, you'll see different perf. we'll tune batch sizes and cache retention policies.
[04:18] Jordan: curious — any regulatory constraints we should know about? data residency?
[04:22] Leon: all EU PII must stay in EU; we have a small EU user base. would need region pinning.
[04:29] Amir: Redwood supports region pinning and can deploy Dedicated pools in EU regions; Private can be on-prem. we'll include that in the security pack.
[04:36] Maya: procurement question — any minimums for Dedicated?
[04:40] Jordan: Dedicated typically has reserved capacity contracts; depends on sizing but we have options for smaller commitments or burstable capacity during pilot. I'll include typical contract sizes.
[04:51] Sara: ok on costs — do you have benchmark examples for 10M tokens/day?
[04:56] Priya: we do; i'll run an estimate but rough math: with optimized quantized setups you can reduce unit costs significantly vs raw openai list pricing; we'll provide a cost model in the pricing sheet.
[05:08] Leon: one more on monitoring — we need tracing down to prompt level for regression analysis.
[05:13] Amir: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and eval hooks. we can expose traces to your datadog or internal systems.
[05:22] Victor: any mention of co-tenancy risks? we prefer dedicated GPU pools.
[05:27] Jordan: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation; Private gives full isolation with customer-managed infra if needed.
[05:32] Sara: what about fallback? if a dedicated pool is saturated, can traffic go to hosted?
[05:36] Priya: yes, smart routing policies can route by latency or cost and have automatic fallback to hosted variants or other model versions.
[05:44] Maya: so next step is benchmark. what output do you need from us?
[05:48] Priya: sample prompt set, traffic distribution (tokens per request histogram), and a list of must-pass prompts for subjective eval. also credentials or s3 with attachments for corpus.
[05:57] Leon: we can provide that by friday.
[06:00] Jordan: perfect. i'll follow up with docs + pricing and Priya will send the benchmark kit.
[06:05] Ethan: one last nit — we run a few custom ops on our runtime, do you support plugin-like custom ops?
[06:10] Priya: we have extension points; for Dedicated/Private we can run custom containers or sidecars to handle pre/post-processing. we'll scope during the SE deep-dive.
[06:22] Jordan: any other blockers?
[06:25] Sara: legal will want the SOC2 and data flow diagrams; procurement will want contract minima.
[06:30] Jordan: we'll include both in the pack.
[06:33] Leon: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:35] Jordan: ok quick recap of action items and timeline...
[06:40] Jordan: recap - Redwood to share price/security pack; customer to send prompts & traffic; schedule SE deep-dive next week; target pilot in Q3.
[06:50] Maya: noted. thanks.
[06:52] Jordan: thanks all, will follow up. bye.
